scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Lost Court Art of Bali

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Gambuh dates to the 15th-century Majapahit era.
It was historically supported by royal courts until their collapse during wars with the Dutch, after which it shifted toward performance at temple ceremonies.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performances are held at temple ceremonies and center on the Malat epic, a narrative about Prince Raden Panji and his search for his fiancée.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The gamelan gambuh ensemble requires approximately 17 musicians.
Key instruments include 75-100 cm bamboo flutes (suling gambuh), a rebab, and unique percussion instruments including the kenyir, kangsi, and gumanak.
Listen for the suling gambuh, rebab, gong, kajar.

The music is defined by the low, resonant tones of 75-100 cm bamboo flutes (suling gambuh) accompanied by a rebab and a specific percussion section including rare instruments like the kenyir and gumanak.

Vocal style: Dialogue in Kawi language, translated to contemporary Balinese.. Form: Gamelan gambuh ensemble.. Mood: sophisticated, epic. It should sound like this: The music is defined by the low, resonant tones of 75-100 cm bamboo flutes (suling gambuh) accompanied by a rebab and a specific percussion section including rare instruments like the kenyir and gumanak. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: neutral dress with a respectful nod (palette and fabric only): the sources describe sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire, or the dance is sacred
care: every element traceable to the costume notes or a licensed image; nothing added for effect
no caricature, no exaggeration, no mixing of regions or eras
a culture bearer reviews the wardrobe before production; the review is recorded in the pack
credits name the tradition and the sources of the reconstruction
